⭐ the fixed engine->track-file entry, called once from engine_init. It arrives WITH the track data (the unpack swap deposits the track file over $5300-$5A25), so it is not a patch site. SILVER: 60 EA EA = RTS/NOP/NOP, a deliberate no-op for the circuit with no hook code. BRANDS: 4C 00 57 = JMP $5700. One call, one target — a far cleaner seam for the port than the five patch sites. ⭐⭐ IN THIS PORT IT IS CORRECTLY A NO-OP FOR EVERY CIRCUIT, and that is not the same as baking Silverstone's RTS by accident: on an expansion circuit $5A22 holds JMP $5700 = ModifyGameCode, whose whole job is to patch the engine, and the port applies that patcher's OUTPUT as data at selection time (tools/track_patch.py replays it; `make track-patch VERIFY=1` cross-checks the replay against a real BBC). Running it here would patch an already-patched image. The guarantee that the replay covered whatever is there is a GENERATION-time one: the replay's interpreter raises on any opcode outside its twelve-form vocabulary. src/platform/track.h, docs/phases.md §5.

the ONLY routine that programs the hardware: 6845 CRTC ($FE00/$FE01), Video ULA palette ($FE21), System VIA T1/ACR/IFR/IER, User VIA T1/ACR/IER. 54 instructions, one caller. This is the platform boundary.

⭐ THE RASTER-BAND PALETTE/MODE SCHEDULE, claimed via IRQ1V — and it DRAWS NOTHING (measured 2026-08-17; it was called 'the 50 Hz game body' until then, and that misnomer is why the row was carried as untouchable engine work). Driven by a USER VIA T1 timeout (LDA $FE6D / AND #$40), NOT System VIA vsync. One PAL field is five interrupts; each arm repaints the ULA mode + palette for the band about to be scanned and reloads the T1 latch with that band's duration — the raster split a BBC has to do on the CPU for want of a copper. Dispatches on irq_band_state; chains to saved_irq1v when the interrupt is not its own. The only game work in the whole cycle is the JSR tick_wheel_spin ($52A4) in band 4: 206-233 us of a 6113 us field, i.e. 4%.

⭐ [DERIVED] THE ENGINE'S DIVIDE, and mul8's opposite number: unsigned (A : math_lo) / shared_temp_76, leaving the 8-bit quotient in math_lo and the remainder in A. Eight unrolled restoring steps, each shifting the 16-bit pair left one place and conditionally subtracting the divisor. Three exit properties a caller can rely on and one it cannot: (a) C is ALWAYS CLEAR on exit — the closing ROL math_lo shifts out the zero the opening ASL inserted, never a quotient bit; (b) N and Z come from the finished quotient; (c) the LAST of the eight steps ($0C9E-$0CA2) computes its quotient bit and then SKIPS the restore, so the returned remainder is the true one PLUS the divisor whenever the quotient is odd; (d) V is left by whichever of the first seven steps subtracted last, which is why the twin replays that one subtract through the 6502's own SBC. A divisor of 0 makes every step subtract nothing and returns a quotient of $FF; a dividend high byte >= the divisor overflows the 8-bit quotient silently — neither happens in the engine, because both callers normalise the divisor until bit 7 is set and branch away on equal magnitudes. 3 callers, all in the road pass: bearing_to_section twice ($21D3, $224B) and project_point once ($22E0). Twin #13, src/gen/revs_native.c. [NAMED 2026-08-17 — was FUN_0c47]

(a) zeroes the horizon extent $1F and calls road_edge_start; (b) sets the far-clip $10/$11 to $FF (unclipped) and the subdivision limit $13 to 13, then runs road_edge_side + road_edge_walk TWICE -- cursor $12 = 6 for one road side and $2E (=6+40) for the other, which is what makes edge_x_lo/hi and edge_y 2x40 arrays; (c) wraps the horizon section index $51 mod 40 into Y, clamps the horizon extent to <= $4E (the 80-entry column space, cf. $18DB LDY #$4F) and writes it back into edge_y[Y] and edge_y[Y+40]; (d) stores |edge_x_hi[Y] - edge_x_hi[Y+40]| / 2 -- half the apparent road width AT THE HORIZON -- into $62FC, read at $1FE4. Stores nothing through (zp),Y: it is compute, not a plotter. ⭐ RENAMED from build_road_edge_lists 2026-08-17: that name was too narrow, not one slot off. The same walk also emits the frame's CORNER MARKERS -- $25D9-$25FB appends up to three into marker_edge_index/marker_flags/marker_offset_lo/hi and INCs marker_count, which the body's 16th call draw_corner_markers consumes and zeroes. So the body's 5th call produces BOTH the edge lists and the marker list, which is what closed the queue's warning about this address.

⭐ [DERIVED] build_track_geometry's first call, and the only part of the road pipeline that REUSES last frame's work. Slots 0..5 of each 40-point half are the edge points beside and behind the car (both walks start at 6) and they are too close to the camera to re-derive, so: (a) if near_edge_scroll_pending is set, shift_near_edge_points slides them up one and the flag is cleared; (b) return at once when near_edge_first or near_edge_last reads 6, the 'nothing owed' sentinel; (c) re-base the surviving slots in PAIRS (slot and slot+40) through rebase_edge_point, which also keeps the horizon maximum; (d) build the ONE new point — near_segment_index picks its track-file segment from (6 - near_edge_cursor)*8 and the player's car_segment wrapped on segment_count_x8 in whichever direction track_direction says, load_section_triple stages it at section index $FD, bearing_to_section + emit_edge_bearing store its angle in BOTH halves, and for the near half only project_point gives it a scan line that is offered to horizon_extent/horizon_index (ties going to the higher slot); (e) hand the next frame the slot below via clamp_near_edge_cursor and clamp horizon_extent to 7 when horizon_index_prev is above 7. ⚠ SMC $231A is a BRANCH OFFSET: $0F skips the re-base pair for the slot the cursor sits on, and every expansion circuit rewrites it to $00 = re-base it anyway. Twin #9, src/gen/revs_native.c.

⭐ [DERIVED] ONE road side, from road_edge_side's section index into the distance: up to 18 edge points (capped at $2498), each stepping further along the section list per edge_walk_step_tbl, so the far half of the road is nearly free. Per point: emit_edge_bearing_at_cursor for the angle and the scaled distance, project_point for the scan line, emit_edge_width_offset for the second angle and any corner marker. Two things make it more than a loop — (1) THE RUNNING NEAREST: a point that beats edge_nearest_lo/hi becomes project_point's far clip and its point count becomes the SUBDIVISION FLOOR; (2) SUBDIVISION: a step that lands behind the camera or past the clip, or one where the road swung more than $14 off the view axis in a single point (and the point before it had not), is replaced by three quarter-way midpoints staged in the section_coord scratch triple at index $FA — one is emitted and the side ends there. A midpoint may NOT append a marker, which is what the marker_count_saved swap is for. section_wrap_limit is what sends the two sides opposite ways round the 120-byte list. ⚠ SMC $248B: Silverstone's BCS/JMP pair becomes one JMP into the circuit's own hook. ⚠ In the transliteration the body is the multi-entry region region_23d8, not one function. Twin #10.

[DERIVED] THE PERSPECTIVE DIVIDE. Takes track section X, subtracts the camera position ($6281/$6284) from the 16-bit value at $0901,X/$0A01,X, takes the absolute value, >>3, and returns CARRY SET if that exceeds point_dist_lo/hi — which point_distance_hypot filled in for THIS SAME point a moment earlier (emit_edge_bearing tail-calls it, and both of road_edge_walk's paths run that before this), so the test is a vertical field-of-view clip against the point's own distance, not a clip against a stale one. Otherwise normalises the distance (the $22C5 shift loop counts the exponent in Y), stashes the reciprocal_table entry and the exponent in proj_width/proj_width_shift for a LATER consumer (neither is read here), then DIVIDES the shifted height by the normalised distance via div16by8 — not multiplies — and forms projected_line = 60 +/- quotient - view_pitch_offset -- the projected screen coordinate in the 0..79 space the edge buffers and column tables use. 3 callers, all inside the road pass. ⚠⚠ IT SHIFTS point_dist_lo IN PLACE: the normalise loop's `ASL $7C` writes the cell back on every pass while the high byte lives only in A, so point_dist_hi survives the call and point_dist_lo does NOT -- anything wanting the true distance must read it before the projection. ⚠ Two entry points, this one forcing Y = 0 (the camera) and falling into project_point_from where Y is the view origin's byte offset. THE EXIT CARRY IS THE RESULT: set means the point was dropped, by the far clip ($22BC) or by an 8-bit quotient running past $80 ($22E7), and three of the four callers branch on it immediately. On the surviving path N is live too ($2401 BPL tests the sign of projected_line); V is dead at every call site. Twin #15, src/gen/revs_native.c.

[DERIVED] which road side the next road_edge_walk emits, and which way round. EORs A with track_direction, so the two calls from build_track_geometry (A=0 and A=$80) always take opposite arms whatever the direction bit holds: one leaves X = section_cursor + $78 with section_wrap_limit = $78, the other X = section_cursor with section_wrap_limit = 0, and the carry that told them apart becomes road_side_index. ⚠ The far arm's CLC/ADC #$78 is the only thing in the routine that writes V and nothing overwrites it before the RTS, so the overflow leaks to the caller. Twin #11.

[PROVISIONAL] how far up the road reaches this frame, in the 0..79 SCAN LINE space the surface_edge buffers, view_paint_lines and project_point all share. road_edge_start keeps it as a running MAXIMUM of project_point's $8D (also maxed in $0BA2 at $0BC3), build_track_geometry clamps it to <= $4E, and it is then the LOOP BOUND for the drawing side: $18BE and $1949 LDY $1F, $31D2 CPY $1F, $1FE9/$66B6 LDX $1F, and surface_colour_at ($1E9E) returns the off-road colour $38FD for anything past it.

[PROVISIONAL] which edge-list entry (0-39) the horizon_extent maximum came from; set alongside $1F at $2398, wrapped mod $28 by build_track_geometry, copied to $52, and read as the base index by $18BC.
[PROVISIONAL] write cursor into edge_x_lo/hi and edge_y. build_track_geometry seeds it 6 for one road side and $2E (=6+40) for the other; road_edge_walk INCs it per point emitted.

[DERIVED] where the FIRST road side's edge points stopped — edge_cursor copied at $2511, i.e. one past the last point of the 0..39 half. build_track_geometry then walks the second side from $2E, so edge_cursor ends inside the 40..79 half and the two cells are the two halves' end cursors. Read exactly once, by draw_road at $1A6F, which pairs it with the 0..39 half's base (horizon_index) for fill_line_attr's second pass — the other pass gets (edge_cursor, horizon_index+$28). Nothing else in the engine touches it.
[DERIVED] low byte of the NEAREST projected distance road_edge_walk has seen this pass; $23E7-$23ED records ($7D,$7C) here whenever the point just projected beats it. Paired with edge_nearest_hi.

[DERIVED] high byte of the same running minimum. build_track_geometry seeds it $FF at $24FF = 'no nearest point yet' (so the first point always wins), which is the sense in which road_edge_walk's note calls $10/$11 a far clip — that note describes the seed, not the cell. ⭐ check_crash ($111E) reads it AFTER the frame's walk and does nothing while it is under 2, and that is ONE quantity, not two (settled 2026-08-17, the queue's '$11 and what check_crash reads it for'): the nearest bit of track being $200 or more away means the car is not on the track, which is exactly the crash condition, and check_crash's next test — |nearest_edge_bearing_hi| against $60 — separates 'off the track ahead' from a real crash.

[DERIVED] the section counter $42 at the moment edge_nearest_lo/hi was last beaten ($23EF-$23F1). road_edge_walk's subdivision test at $246D only fires once $42 passes it, so seeding it — build_track_geometry writes $0D at $2503 — is what makes the walk emit at least 13 sections before it starts interpolating midpoints. (Called 'the point count cap' in road_edge_walk's note, which is the same gate seen from the seed site.)

[DERIVED] the PREVIOUS frame's horizon_index, wrapped mod 40 — build_track_geometry stores it at $2529 as the last thing it does, and the only reader is road_edge_start at $23B2-$23B8 on the NEXT frame, which clamps horizon_extent down to 7 when it exceeds 7. A one-frame history cell, not a scratch copy.

[PROVISIONAL] half the apparent road width at the horizon: |edge_x_hi[horizon_index] - edge_x_hi[horizon_index+40]| >> 1, written by build_track_geometry ($2546) and compared at $1FE4. The only two references in the engine.

column1: ## build_track_geometry's three callees.  $2145 is an ARCTAN (quadrant bases $20/$60/$A0/$E0
## $0BA2 re-bases an already-emitted point by the very delta integrate_car_position adds to
## the heading.  So edge_x is the point's azimuth relative to where the car is pointing
## interp_edge is what turns an azimuth into a column.  ⚠ That is also what proved $000A/$000B
## a HEADING rather than a position
column2: and they were renamed car_heading_lo/hi for it.

column5: [DERIVED] THE BEARING, and the first half of every edge point. Takes section byte index X, subtracts the camera position ($6280-$6285) from the section's +0 and +2 coordinate pairs, takes both absolute values, divides the smaller by the larger (div16by8, after normalising the larger until its high byte has bit 7 set), looks the ratio up in arctan_table and adds the quadrant base -- leaving the 16-bit angle in bearing_lo/hi and the raw table byte in shared_temp_7e, which is what point_distance_hypot then picks its segment on. The two deltas land in point_delta_lo/hi/sign components 0 and 2, and the sorted magnitudes in hypot_min_lo/hi and hypot_max_lo/hi. The degenerate arm ($220D) returns one of four 45-degree diagonals ($20/$60/$E0/$A0 on the two sign bits) and shared_temp_7e = $FF; it is reached three ways -- equal magnitudes ($21B8), or either arm's normalised dividend catching up with the divisor ($21D1, $2249) -- and never divides, so div16by8's flags cannot reach the exit through it. ⚠⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-18: this note used to say the two arms scale the arctan differently, 'the arm at $21DC shifts it 3 places and the one at $2254 shifts it 1'. Both have exactly THREE LSR/ROR pairs ($21E1-$21EA and $2259-$2262), so both scale by 32 and 45 degrees reads $1FE0 on either. What actually differs is the octant: the quadrant BASE ($40/$C0 off component 0's sign against $00/$80 off component 2's) and the DIRECTION of the negate (arm A negates when the two signs agree, arm B when they differ). Counted out of the listing, not read out of the prose. ⚠ Two entry points: this one forces Y = 0 (the camera) and falls into bearing_to_section_from, where Y is the view origin's byte offset. No caller reads any exit flag -- all four do LDY/LDA immediately -- but A and Y are both live (A = bearing_hi, Y = the quotient except on the degenerate arm). Twin #14, src/gen/revs_native.c.

[DERIVED] stores bearing_lo/hi - car_heading into edge_x_lo/hi at index Y -- the point's angle RELATIVE TO WHERE THE CAR IS POINTING -- then tail-calls point_distance_hypot, which leaves the point's scaled distance in point_dist_lo/hi. road_edge_start calls it directly at $2374 with Y already chosen.
[DERIVED] bearing_to_section + emit_edge_bearing at index edge_cursor. road_edge_walk's per-point entry ($23D8 for a section point, $2452 for an interpolated midpoint).
[DERIVED] the two per-wing constant coefficients scale_wing_settings multiplies each (setting*4) by ($0B80) on the way to wing_grip_coeff. Two bytes, front then rear.

[DERIVED] copies a section's HEIGHT component (component 1) from road-edge side 0 (section_coord_lo/hi[X+1]) to side 1 (section_coord_lo/hi[X+$79]). The two road edges share the same height, so after FUN_12f7/FUN_122d build side 1's ground-plane pair (components 0 and 2 = side 0 + across-track normal) this fills in its height by a plain copy. X = section byte cursor. No escaping flags. Twin #139. Was FUN_124d.

[INFERRED] zero-page cache of the CURRENT track segment's field-0 flags byte, loaded from track_segment_lo[Y] at $1326 (FUN_1267). Two uses: bit 0 gates advance_dir_on_segment_flag ($13DA), which steps segment_dir_index when set; and the whole byte is ANDed into the section_flags entry the road builder writes at $137C. Field 0 of the 8-byte segment record (fields 1..3 are coordinates, 7 is segment length).

[DERIVED] tiny dispatcher: if bit 0 of cur_segment_flags is set, calls step_segment_dir_index ($13E0) to advance segment_dir_index; otherwise calls FUN_13fa (the Silverstone RTS no-op the expansion circuits patch). Reached via the $13C9/$1426 per-circuit SMC dispatch. Preserves X; callers discard the exit flags. Twin #143. Was FUN_13da.

[DERIVED] steps segment_dir_index one track position along the direction tables, wrapping at track_dir_count, in whichever direction track_direction's bit 7 selects: forward idx+1 (wraps to 0 at the count), backward idx-1 (wraps 0 to count-1). Tail-calls FUN_13fa (a Silverstone RTS no-op the expansion circuits patch). Preserves X; callers ($1289 SMC dispatch, $13DA) discard the exit flags. Twin #142. Was FUN_13e0.

[DERIVED] builds the signed 16-bit 3-component step delta that section_coord_add_delta integrates into a section's coordinate: sign-extends track_dir_0/1/2[Y] (components 0/2 the ground plane, |.|=$78; component 1 the small gradient) into 16-bit values with low bytes in math_lo/math_hi/shared_temp_76 and high bytes in point_delta_hi[0..2]. When track_direction != 0 (running the track backwards) each component is two's-complement negated. D=0 on this path. Callers ($1335, $2A11) discard the exit registers/flags. Twin #141. Was FUN_1442.

[DERIVED] maps the walk-origin section_cursor to car_section_cursor: computes section_cursor - $60 and, if that goes negative, wraps by adding $78 (the 40-section x 3-byte ring), so the result lands in 0..$77. D=0 on this path (binary subtract). Called from $13D3, which discards the exit flags. Twin #140. Was FUN_125a.

[DERIVED] integrates one signed 3-component direction delta into a section's 16-bit coordinates: for each component i=0..2, section_coord[X+i] = section_coord[Y+i] + delta[i], where delta[i] = {point_delta_hi[i] : (math_lo,math_hi,shared_temp_76)[i]} taken as a signed 16-bit. FUN_12f7 the road builder calls it with Y=section_cursor_prev, X=section_cursor to make section N's point from section N-1's plus the step FUN_1442 built; place_car_world_coords's AI branch reuses it on the scratch section slots $09F4/$09FA/$09FD. Three independent 16-bit adds, no escaping flags. Twin #138. Was FUN_0bcc.

[DERIVED] re-bases one ALREADY-EMITTED edge point Y for this frame's camera motion instead of re-walking it: zeroes $5EE0,Y, subtracts model_state element 2 ($62D2/$62E2 -- the same delta integrate_car_position adds to car_heading) from edge_x_lo/hi, subtracts $4E from edge_y, and keeps the result's running maximum in horizon_extent/horizon_index. road_edge_start runs it over the near slots as a PAIR (slot and slot+40) at $2323/$2328.

[DERIVED] copies one 3-byte coordinate triple out of the TRACK FILE ($5901,Y-$5903,Y low, $5301,Y-$5303,Y high) into section_coord_lo/hi at X. Y is a segment byte index, X the destination section byte index. $122D is the longer entry that also takes the segment's second triple.

[INFERRED] slides the five NEAR edge slots of each 40-point half up by one (entry i -> i+1 for i = $2C..$28 and 4..0 of edge_x_lo, edge_x_hi and edge_y), freeing slot 0 and slot $28 for the newest point, then sets near_edge_first = 6 - near_edge_shift and clamps the window ($12C8). Run once per section step, gated on near_edge_scroll_pending.
[INFERRED] raises near_edge_last by one (capped at 6, floored at near_edge_first), then falls into clamp_near_edge_cursor with X = near_edge_cursor + 1.

[INFERRED] entered with a candidate slot in X (which it INCs first): lowers near_edge_last to that when it is higher, then snaps the slot to 5 if it falls outside [near_edge_first, 5] and stores it as near_edge_cursor. road_edge_start's tail calls it with near_edge_cursor - 1, i.e. hands the next frame the slot below this one.

[INFERRED] the second half of every edge point road_edge_walk emits. Reads the section's flags byte out of section_flags (via $0702,X or the $068A alias for X >= $78), masks it with $306C[road_side_index], turns the low 3 bits into a shift from $306E, and stores edge_x +/- (proj_width scaled by proj_width_shift) into edge_opp_x_lo/hi -- the OPPOSITE road boundary's azimuth at the same point, sign from road_side_index vs track_direction. It emits nothing at all for the walk's first three points ($2580-$2586, $42 < 3). ⚠ It ALSO appends up to three CORNER MARKERS ($25D9-$25FB: marker_edge_index / marker_flags / marker_offset, INCing marker_count) when flag bits 3-4 are set, which is how the body's 5th call comes to produce the marker list the 16th call consumes.

[DERIVED] FIELD 2 of the 3-byte per-section record at $0700-$0777 -- section_dir_index is field 0 and section_curve field 1, and section_cursor is a BYTE index stepping by 3 and wrapping at $78, so the page holds 40 sections and not 120 independent entries (CORRECTED 2026-08-18 with twins #98-#114; the three rows used to read as three overlapping 120-entry tables, which is impossible). Per-section feature flags, indexed the same way as section_cursor. $068A is the SAME table addressed as $0702 - $78, which is how $2567-$2570 indexes it with X mod $78 in two instructions. Bits 0-2 index BOTH edge_style_tbl ($306E, the point's surface style) and edge_width_shift_tbl ($3076, the exponent the width offset is shifted by), bit 0 also halves a corner marker's offset, bits 3-4 mean 'a corner marker belongs here'. $129C zeroes the current entry.

[DERIVED] low bytes of the LIVE section geometry: 40 sections x 3 bytes = $78 = 120, addressed by section_cursor. Each section owns three 16-bit values (+0/+1/+2) whose high bytes are section_coord_hi; bearing_to_section takes its arctan from +0 and +2, project_point divides +1. load_section_triple fills one from the track file. ⚠ SECOND HALF: byte cursors $78..$EF address a PARALLEL 40-section list — the OPPOSITE road edge — whose ground-plane pair (components 0,2) FUN_12f7/FUN_122d build as side 0 plus the across-track normal ($5700/$5800) and whose height (component 1) is copied across by copy_section_height_to_side1; road_edge_side_apply starts one walk at cursor and the other at cursor+$78. ⚠ Indices $FA and $FD are SCRATCH, not sections -- $09FA is where road_edge_walk interpolates its three midpoints and $09FD where road_edge_start stages the near point.
the high bytes of section_coord_lo.

[DERIVED] 18 entries: how far along the section list road_edge_walk steps for point N ($249C LDA $3DD0,Y with Y = the point counter, bounded at $12 = 18 by $2498). The step grows with distance, which is what makes the far half of the road cheap.

[DERIVED] bit 7 = which way round the circuit the car is going. $1424 is the ONLY writer and it FLIPS the bit (LDA $25 / EOR #$80 / STA $25). Read as a sign: road_edge_side ($254C) picks the traversal origin with it, road_edge_start branches on it twice ($2338 wrap direction, $236C which half of the edge arrays), emit_edge_width_offset picks the offset's sign, and build_player_car EORs it into car_heading_hi. Only the sign bit is ever used.

[DERIVED] the player's cursor into section_coord_lo/hi, in BYTES: 40 sections x 3, wrapped at $78 = 120. $12F7 steps it forward by 3 (saving the old value in section_cursor_prev) and $140B steps it back; road_edge_side reads it as the origin of each side's walk.
[DERIVED] the previous section_cursor, saved at $12F9 before the step.

[DERIVED] what road_edge_walk's step wraps against ($24A1-$24AD: if X - this >= step then X -= step, else X += $78 first). road_edge_side sets it to 0 for one road side and $78 = 120 for the other, which is what makes the two sides walk the section list in opposite directions off the same cursor.

[DERIVED] which road side the current walk is emitting, 0 or 1 -- road_edge_side's carry captured with LDA #0 / ROL A at $255F. emit_edge_width_offset uses it to index $306C and, re-read at $25AB, to pick the width offset's sign.

[DERIVED] the TRACK-FILE segment byte index road_edge_start hands load_section_triple for the near edge point. Computed at $2330-$235C from (6 - near_edge_cursor) * 8 and the player's own car_segment ($06FF), wrapped on segment_count_x8 in whichever direction track_direction says; $23A3 adds 3 for the pass that wants the segment's SECOND triple.

[INFERRED] first of the six NEAR edge slots (0..5 of each 40-point half) that still needs rebuilding this frame; 6 = none, and road_edge_start returns immediately on it. Those slots are the points beside and behind the car -- both walks start at 6 -- so they are SCROLLED by shift_near_edge_points rather than re-walked, and near_edge_first/near_edge_last bound how many of them the section step invalidated. $12BD sets it to 6 - near_edge_shift.

[INFERRED] the last of those slots, 6 = none (also a bail-out for road_edge_start). Clamped into [near_edge_first, 6] by clamp_near_edge_window / clamp_near_edge_cursor, forced to 6 by $13FB (a heading change big enough that nothing is reusable) and seeded 6 at race init ($1880).
[INFERRED] how far shift_near_edge_points slid the near slots, i.e. how many sections the player crossed. $1290 stores it as a value ANDed with 7; $12BD turns it into near_edge_first = 6 - it.

[DERIVED] which near edge slot road_edge_start re-projects this frame: $235E seeds the point counter with it and the loop runs for that slot and slot+40. clamp_near_edge_cursor writes it at the end of every pass, and $23AC-$23AF hands the next frame the slot below.

[INFERRED] non-zero = the near edge points have not been scrolled for the section step yet. road_edge_start runs shift_near_edge_points and clears it at $22FF-$2309; $126B sets it (to 6, not 1 -- it shares the LDY #6 that also forces near_edge_last).

⚠ SHARED SCRATCH -- ten writers ($0D10 $10F0 $11D2 $1429 $1DEF $2360 $23D6 $28F7 $2A30 $2A39) and no one meaning, which is why nothing can rename it. In the road-geometry pass it is the walk's POINT COUNTER: road_edge_start seeds it with near_edge_cursor and steps it by $28 so the loop runs the slot and slot+40, road_edge_walk zeroes it at $23D6 and INCs it per point emitted, edge_nearest_section records it, and $2498 caps the walk at $12 = 18 points.

[DERIVED] the section byte index road_edge_walk emitted a point from LAST time ($2490 STX $14). Its subdivision arm interpolates three midpoints between it and the current index ($240C LDY $14), and $245A restores X from it before emitting the midpoint.
[DERIVED] the edge_cursor at the moment road_edge_walk last beat edge_nearest_lo/hi ($23F3-$23F5). Paired with nearest_edge_bearing_hi.
[DERIVED] edge_x_hi at that same nearest point ($23F7-$23FA) -- the azimuth of the closest bit of track this pass found.

[DERIVED] low byte of the 16-bit DISTANCE point_distance_hypot leaves for the point just transformed. road_edge_walk compares it against edge_nearest_lo/hi ($23DB-$23E5) to keep the running nearest, and project_point divides by the same pair ($22B0-$22BA, and $22E0) -- one reading, the CURRENT point's distance, written by point_distance_hypot before either reader runs. ⚠ Six unrelated writers ($1C2C $1CF4 $1D1A $1D39 $1D84 apply_angle_term $48C9) reuse the cell outside the road pass, so a value reading only holds between the hypot and the projection.
high byte of point_dist_lo.
[DERIVED] low byte of the 16-bit bearing bearing_to_section computes from the camera to a section point. emit_edge_bearing turns it into an edge_x entry by subtracting car_heading.
high byte of bearing_lo; the quadrant base ($20/$60/$A0/$E0, or $40/$C0 on the degenerate arm) lands here.

[DERIVED] the SCAN LINE (the 0..79 space horizon_extent shares) project_point's perspective divide leaves for the point it was given ($22FB). road_edge_start copies it into BOTH halves of edge_y and keeps its running maximum in horizon_extent / horizon_index.

[DERIVED] marker_count saved and restored around road_edge_walk's INTERPOLATED-midpoint emit ($245C-$2465), which is how a midpoint gets its second angle out of emit_edge_width_offset without being allowed to append a corner marker. ⚠ $1B1B stores an unrelated Y here.

⚠ SHARED SCRATCH in the $74-$79 arithmetic window. road_edge_walk's subdivision arm parks the current section index here across the three-component interpolation loop ($240E, $2445-$244B); emit_edge_width_offset ($2576) and $134F use it for unrelated bytes; and build_sign_origin uses it as a COMPONENT INDEX, seeded to 2 by build_road_sign at $4CBE and DECed on each of its three calls. Four unrelated owners settles the fact-shaped name -- no single meaning covers them, same as shared_temp_76 / shared_temp_7e / shared_temp_8c / shared_temp_8e.
⚠ revs_mem.bin ONLY. Copies $1200-$12FF to $7900 and runs from the copy. In the runtime image this address holds relocated engine code instead.

THE SECOND UNPACK. Assembles $7B00-$7FFF (1280 bytes of code) plus the dashboard bitmap out of the tails of 41 dashData blocks spaced $80 apart from $3000. $192F seeds $70-$73 = src $3000 / dst base $7FB0; $3900,X is block X's start offset; the destination DESCENDS to $7768. Bit 7 of A set = run in reverse and stow the code back before switching to MODE 7 — which is why the page is empty in every static image. tools/dashdata.py replays it. See docs/static-map.md open item 6.

41 bytes — dashData block X's start offset within its $80-byte block, read as $3900,X by copy_dash_data ($190E) and by the fill loop at $31D0. Data always ENDS at offset $4F. Also read by the rasteriser ($1C94, $1DF5, $2FF5).

⭐⭐ [DERIVED] THE 3D VIEWPORT RASTERISER — the biggest main-loop item in the port (30.5% / 131 ms, docs/perf-method.md). It paints ONE SCAN LINE PER CHAIN, top down: $70/$71 = $6700 and $72/$73 = $6800, and $6700 - BBC_SCREEN_BASE ($5A80) = 3200 = 10*320 exactly, i.e. character row 10 / cell 0 / line 0 = DISPLAY LINE 80, while $6800 = $6700+256 is cell 32 of the same row. So the 40 chain units are the 40 CELLS ACROSS a line (unit i writes base + 8*i, and cells 32-39 come off the second pointer because 40*8 = 320 > 256), and X = $4F..$03 is the line, stepped by $7EF3 (+1 within a character row, +$139 across one). Confirmed independently on a real BBC: stores cover display lines 80..157, buckets 88..111 full at 320 = 8 lines x 40 cells (`make fbwrites`). Each unit is `LDY srcTable,X / BEQ / LDA #0 / STA srcTable,X / LDA $6000,Y / LDY #cell*8 / STA (zp),Y` over the $80-spaced source blocks $3000..$4380 — one block per CELL COLUMN, indexed by line — and A carries left to right, so a zero source means 'same byte as the cell to my LEFT'. THREE phases by how much of the line is painted: phase 1 ($7BE2, X=$4F..$2C) all 40 cells; phases 2 ($7D13, X=$2B..$1C) and 3 ($7F18, X=$1B..$03) plant an RTS to stop the chain at a per-line cell and compose the boundary byte themselves — the silhouette of the cockpit opening. Measured: 2093 units run per sweep for ~83 changed bytes (docs/direct-bitplane-plan.md §7a). Self-modifying by construction — 42 patch sites, docs/static-map.md §Open items 10.

view_paint_lines phase 2 (X=$2B..$1C): plants the chain-A stop RTS from $3150,X and the chain-B start from $30D0,X, runs the chain, then composes the two boundary bytes itself. Reached only by falling out of $7BE2.

view_paint_lines phase 3 (X=$1B..$03): as phase 2 but plants BOTH chains' stop cells ($3150,X and $3080,X) and both start offsets, and steps the scan-line pointers itself instead of via $7EF3. Reached only from $7D13; exits through view_paint_restore.

view_paint_lines' exit: puts `STA` ($91) back over the three RTS opcodes the sweep planted (the slots recorded in $7D24/$7F24/$7F7D) and `CPX` ($E0) back at $7EEE, leaving the chain unpatched for the next call.

TWIN #3 (src/gen/revs_native.c): a native DRIVER — the three restart targets are a nested RestartDepth, the tail is a LoopVerdict, and both port hooks are spelled out by hand because the transpiler emits them only into the oracle.
